title: Geometry & Mensuration
tagline: Triangles, circles, solids, trig, coordinate geometry — draw first, formula second.

subsections.title: Triangles
subsections.trick: Apollonius’ Theorem is the fastest route to a median length — don’t drop a perpendicular and use Pythagoras twice. For area, pick the formula that matches what’s given: base+height, all 3 sides (Heron), two sides+included angle, or inradius+semi-perimeter.

Right angle at A — leg AB
Right angle at A — leg AC

subsections.title: Polygons
subsections.trick: Exterior angles of any convex polygon always sum to 360° regardless of the number of sides — use that before the interior-angle formula, it's one less step.

subsections.title: Circles
subsections.trick: Power-of-a-point (PA×PB = PC×PD, or PT² for a tangent) solves almost every ‘two chords/tangent meet outside a circle’ question in one line — no need to find angles first. Count common tangents by picturing the two-circle case: apart →4, intersecting →2, internally touching →1, one inside the other →0.

subsections.title: Mensuration — 2D Figures
subsections.trick: For a trapezium/quadrilateral with a diagonal + two altitudes given, split into two triangles rather than hunting for a single formula — the table formula is just that split pre-done.

formulas.label: Path across the middle of a rectangle

subsections.title: Mensuration — Solids
subsections.trick: Volume scales with the cube of linear size, surface area with the square — if a solid is scaled by k, volume ×k³ and surface area ×k². Saves recomputing from scratch on ‘melted and recast’ questions.

formulas.label: Right prism
formulas.latex: LSA = (\text{perimeter of base})\times h, \quad V = (\text{area of base})\times h

formulas.label: Right circular cylinder
formulas.latex: LSA = 2\pi rh, \quad TSA = 2\pi r(r+h), \quad V = \pi r^2 h

formulas.label: Right pyramid
formulas.latex: LSA = \tfrac{1}{2}(\text{perimeter of base})\times(\text{slant height}), \quad V = \tfrac{1}{3}(\text{area of base})\times h

formulas.label: Right circular cone
formulas.latex: LSA=\pi r\ell, \quad TSA=\pi r(\ell+r), \quad V=\tfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h, \quad \ell=\sqrt{r^2+h^2}

formulas.label: Hemisphere
formulas.latex: LSA=2\pi r^2, \quad TSA=3\pi r^2, \quad V=\tfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3

subsections.title: Trigonometry
subsections.trick: “School | After — To | College”: reading the 2×2 quadrant grid like a page, that's the order All / Sin / Tan / Cos are positive going anticlockwise from Q1. For standard angles, know sin·cos·tan at 0°/30°/45°/60°/90° cold — deriving them costs too much time mid-exam.

formulas.label: tan in terms of sin, cos

subsections.title: Coordinate Geometry
subsections.trick: The shoelace-style area formula works even when the triangle looks 'obviously' irregular — no need to identify base/height on a coordinate grid. For perpendicular distance from the origin specifically, skip x₁,y₁ entirely and use c/√(a²+b²) directly.
